name: Kailasa Temple, Ellora
scope: Standing rock-cut Kailasa Temple, Cave 16, Ellora, covering the monolithic sanctuary, Nandi pavilion, entrance gate, elephant plinth, detached shrines and rock court with its enclosing cliffs.
era: Present surviving Cave 16, including the roof and open court above its surviving ancient carvings.

references.caption: Archaeological site of Monolithic Cave and Temple ruins in Maharashtra, India
references.alt: Archaeological site of Monolithic Cave and Temple ruins in Maharashtra, India

originalReview.notes: Amitbalani’s exact exterior courtyard photograph resolves the stacked stone terraces, elephant plinth and high carved side gallery with a vertical rock scarp.
K.Venkataramana’s exact outdoor wall view resolves the layered carved panel bands, gray-brown basalt and the relief depth along the lower sanctuary facade.

review.method: Exact CC0 Qualla wall and courtyard photos, mapped native envelope, documented measurements and original terrain
review.notes: Both exact Qualla images document the actual standing Cave 16 court facades and stone reliefs. Other exact public-domain images show Cave 10 or a different rear cave and were excluded. Physical dimensions and arrangement follow the State Party’s conservation report. The original elevation field is retained as the review baseline but is too coarse to encode the open excavation.
